title: Expand anonymous edge caching and normalize discovery response freshness

endpoints.before: Anonymous offer-position requests always forwarded upstream despite the five-minute CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing five-minute CDN TTL. Entries retain the offer ID, full query and Origin; hits avoid origin processing, including origin rate limits and anti-abuse checks. Gateway access checks, credential/range exclusions, CORS, client freshness headers and response schemas are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous offer-asset requests always forwarded upstream despite the five-minute CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing five-minute CDN TTL. Entries retain the offer ID, full query and Origin; hits avoid origin processing, including origin rate limits and anti-abuse checks. Gateway access checks, credential/range exclusions, CORS, client freshness headers and response schemas are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous price requests always reached the origin, including its offer eligibility lookup before Redis, despite the five-minute CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing five-minute CDN TTL. Offer ID, country and all query parameters remain in the key, partitioned by Origin. Requests carrying cookies, user authorization, session tokens or ranges bypass the cache; only shareable successful responses are stored. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Response schemas, country validation and gateway access requirements are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous top-seller requests always forwarded upstream despite the one-hour CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing one-hour CDN TTL. Full query keys preserve locale, page, limit and expansion, and entries are partitioned by Origin. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Gateway access checks, credential/range exclusions, CORS, freshness headers and response schemas are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous free-game requests always forwarded upstream despite the five-minute CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing five-minute CDN TTL. Full query keys preserve country, locale and expansion; entries are partitioned by Origin. Cookie-selected countries, user authorization, session tokens and ranges bypass caching. Only shareable successful responses are stored. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Response schemas, CORS and gateway access requirements are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous free-game statistics always forwarded upstream despite the 24-hour CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing 24-hour CDN TTL. Country and all query parameters remain in the key, partitioned by Origin; cookie/session/authorization/range exclusions remain in place. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Response schemas, CORS, client freshness headers and gateway access requirements are preserved. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous GET searches always forwarded upstream despite the five-minute CDN policy.
endpoints.after: Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD searches use the isolated public Worker cache with the existing five-minute CDN TTL. All search, country, locale, pagination, sort and expansion query parameters remain in the key, partitioned by Origin; repeated query-value ordering is preserved. Credential/range exclusions and non-shareable response exclusions remain in place. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Request validation, response schemas and gateway access requirements are preserved. POST redirects are unchanged. Requires Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Anonymous homepage statistics always forwarded upstream. Redis hits advertised a one-hour browser TTL while freshly computed responses had no explicit cache freshness.
endpoints.after: Successful fresh and Redis-cached responses consistently advertise 60-second browser freshness and five-minute shared freshness. Responses without an explicit country now vary on Cookie, preserving EGDATA_COUNTRY selection and excluding those responses from Worker storage. Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests with an explicit country use the isolated public Worker cache. Full queries and Origin variants remain distinct; credentials, cookies and ranges bypass caching. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Body schemas and country resolution are unchanged; existing country inputs and new cache headers are documented in OpenAPI. Requires origin and Worker deployment.

endpoints.before: Autocomplete used Redis without explicit HTTP freshness, and anonymous requests always forwarded upstream.
endpoints.after: Successful fresh and Redis-cached responses consistently advertise 60-second browser and CDN freshness. Eligible anonymous GET/HEAD requests use the isolated public Worker cache with query, locale, limit and all other query parameters retained, partitioned by Origin. Credential/range exclusions and non-shareable response exclusions remain in place. Hits avoid origin processing and its per-request checks. Request validation, response schemas, CORS and gateway access requirements are preserved. Requires origin and Worker deployment.
